_: Meshy's community pieces (CC0; docs/research/meshy-library.md, meshy-pulls.md) brought into the game by realm/tools/meshy_import.py (Blender, headless, CPU): each piece read from its download folder (src, under ~/code/goc-kits/meshy/), joined into one mesh, turned (yaw: degrees about the vertical, so its front faces +Z, our street side), stood on the ground and centred, scaled to its true size (height_m, metres), cut to its triangle budget (tris), and its house-colour faces (roofs, awnings: by hue in its painted texture, or its material's colour) split into their own material named MI_RoundTiles_house, which team_colour.gd tints with the holder's colour as it does a kit roof; mask.png beside it is the same mask as a texture. Written to realm/assets/meshy/<name>/<name>.glb with import.json (what it did). In play (--landmarks=meshy or landmarks here, realistic.gd): a piece's file, once it stands, takes the place of the catalogue component it names (replaces) in towns; so the catapult takes the siege camp's catapult (it has no arm to swing: its stone leaves from its top) and the guard tower the camp's parked siege tower. A piece not yet imported changes nothing. mask: hues ([from, to] degrees, wrapping 360), sat_min, val_min (0-1); up_min: a face that must also face up this much to count (roofs: 0.25; awnings and banners: -1, any way). defaults: for a piece that doesn't say.
_cuts: smoke_above: loose parts above this share of the height that are grey are cut (Meshy painted chimney smoke as solid grey blobs; the game draws its own). cut: boxes [[x0,y0,z0],[x1,y1,z1]] in metres (the import's frame, z up) whose faces are cut. repaint: [{box, light_above, colour, flat}] (flat: the whole region its median colour, and its normal map flat; match gold: only gold texels, to the rest's median): pale faces in a box (a cream glyph: the cart's money-bag '$') painted plain. flatten: [{axis, centre, radius, to, out}] presses a raised emblem flat. passage: {box, colour}: a way through where a gate was cut open (floor, sides, ceiling facing in; Meshy's models are a hollow shell). realm/tools/meshy_measure.py draws a piece over a numbered metre grid to read these. arm: {box, pivot, tip}: those faces made the throwing arm (its own node, named arm, origin at the pivot, local -X toward the tip), for siege_camp.gd to swing. realm/tools/meshy_import.py -- <name> --islands lists the loose parts to find them.
_judged: Each piece judged in a Blender CPU turntable (realm/tools/meshy_turntable.py) before wiring: judged says why. Passed and wired: forge, lumber mill, catapult, guard tower, gatehouse (castle_gate: castle_builder.gd), market cart (square_cart: the crown's market carter, town_life.gd), tavern (30,000 tris, its smoke cut). Held: market stalls (a shed welded on). Rejected: treasury, house, well.

treasury.judged: rejected: a dollar sign on its gable and strongroom door, not of this realm. 2026-11-12 fix tried (door sliver cut; front coin pressed flat and painted, back coin gold-matched): the front glyph still reads faintly and the back coin is untouched, so it stays out

gatehouse.judged: passed: clean hand-painted stone and timber, an arched gate, 01-town's look

house.judged: rejected: at 30,000 tris it holds, but cutting its grey smoke took dark roof parts with it (holes along the ridge); needs its smoke cut by hand, and its tankard sign off (a second inn). 2026-11-12 measured again: at 30000 tris the roofs are ragged, the smoke cut leaves a black hole in the ridge and the walls are flecked white; with its tankard sign and barrels it is a second inn beside the tavern. Stays out; the kit houses stay

tavern.judged: passed at 30,000 tris (from 1.3M): clean timber frame and shingles, its tankard sign; the solid grey chimney smoke cut (smoke_above)

well.judged: rejected: even at 6,000 tris its shingles are loose cards standing off the roof

market_cart.judged: passed: crisp, a striped awning, lanterns, goods

market_stalls.judged: passed: clean at 30,000 tris, its welded shed cut away (cut): four striped stalls with their goods on a cobbled base, 7.8 x 6.7 m; a whole market block, not single stalls, so unplaced until the square gives it a place
